name: Stir-Frying
description: High-heat, quick cooking in a wok; requires velveting or cutting ingredients small for rapid, even cooking

name: Deep-Frying
description: Submerging food in hot oil; developed independently in multiple cultures; Japanese tempura via Portuguese

name: Sautéing
description: Quick cooking in shallow fat over high heat; foundation of French culinary technique

name: Fermentation
description: Microbial transformation of food; discovered independently worldwide; includes kimchi, sauerkraut, miso, injera

name: Pickling
description: Preserving food in acidic solution (vinegar) or lacto-fermentation; essential before refrigeration

name: Smoking
description: Exposing food to smoke for preservation and flavor; one of the oldest food preservation methods

name: Salt Curing
description: Using salt to draw moisture from food for preservation; basis of prosciutto, bacalao, salt cod

name: Tandoor Cooking
description: Cooking in cylindrical clay oven at extreme heat (480°C); naan bread and tandoori chicken

name: Wood-Fired Oven
description: Brick or stone oven heated by wood fire; essential for Neapolitan pizza and artisan breads

name: Pit Roasting
description: Cooking in earth pit with heated stones; includes Mexican barbacoa, Peruvian pachamanca, Hawaiian imu

name: Steaming
description: Cooking with steam from boiling water; Chinese bamboo steamers; gentle technique preserving nutrients

name: Braising
description: Searing then slow-cooking in liquid; foundation of French pot-au-feu, Chinese red-cooking, Korean jjim

name: Slow Cooking/Stewing
description: Long, low-heat cooking in liquid; tagines, curries, goulash; earliest form of complex cooking

name: Grilling/Broiling
description: Direct heat cooking over flame; oldest cooking technique; includes yakitori, kebab, asado, satay

name: Charcoal Grilling
description: Using charcoal for controlled, intense heat; Japanese binchotan, Turkish mangal, Korean gogigui

name: Wok Hei
description: Breath of the wok — charred flavor from extreme wok heat; requires temperatures above 1200°C at wok surface

name: Tempering/Tadka
description: Blooming spices in hot oil/ghee then pouring over dish; foundation of Indian flavor development

name: Nixtamalization
description: Treating maize with alkaline solution (lime water); unlocks niacin and creates masa; prevents pellagra

name: Sushi-Making
description: Evolved from narezushi (fermented fish preservation) to modern vinegared rice with fresh fish; years of training required

name: Pasta Making
origin_culture: Independent: Chinese noodles and Italian pasta
description: Flour-and-water dough shaped and cooked; Chinese lamian and Italian pasta developed independently

name: Bread Making
description: Leavened bread from wild yeast; foundation of civilization; each culture developed distinct traditions

name: Wok Smoking
description: Tea-smoking in a wok with tea leaves, rice, and sugar; Sichuan smoked duck technique

name: Sous Vide
description: Vacuum-sealed cooking in precise water bath; invented 1970s; revolutionized professional kitchens

name: Ceviche/Acid Cooking
description: Denaturing proteins with citrus acid instead of heat; pre-Columbian technique refined with Old World limes

name: Curry Paste Pounding
description: Grinding fresh aromatics (chilies, lemongrass, galangal) in mortar and pestle; foundation of Southeast Asian curries

name: Drying/Dehydration
description: Sun-drying, air-drying, or oven-drying to preserve food; jerky, dried pasta, sun-dried tomatoes, dried fish

name: Emulsification
description: Combining immiscible liquids (oil and water) into stable mixtures; mayonnaise, vinaigrettes, beurre blanc

name: Dim Sum/Dumpling Wrapping
description: Wrapping fillings in dough; evolved independently into gyoza, manti, pierogi, ravioli, khinkali, momo

name: Rotisserie
description: Slow-rotating meat on spit over fire; Turkish döner, Greek gyros, French rotisserie all descend from this

name: Clay Pot Cooking
description: Cooking in unglazed clay vessels; tagine, biryani, donabe; clay imparts unique flavor and retains moisture
